name: Kroma
tagline: The README says MIT. The repo tag — and the merged base weights — say otherwise
description: Lodestones — the community fine-tuner behind the Chroma line — retrains Krea 2 into Kroma, with the Krea 2 Turbo delta merged in as a rank-512 LoRA. v0.2 abandons the v0.1 LoRA-plus-diff packaging for a single full checkpoint: load it in any recent ComfyUI with native Krea 2 support (Qwen3-VL text encoder + VAE), sample at 8–12 steps, CFG 1.0–1.5.
why: It's the fastest-moving community checkpoint in the Krea 2 ecosystem, and it's this week's textbook licensing case: the README declares MIT for the fine-tune while explicitly granting no rights to the base weights — which are physically inside the merged checkpoint you download. The file you get is governed by the Krea 2 Community License, and the HF tag says exactly that.
useCases: ComfyUI image workflows on the Krea 2 stack with turbo-speed sampling
Community fine-tune and LoRA experimentation on a current-gen base
A case study in how licenses actually propagate through merged checkpoints
audience: ComfyUI users, fine-tuners — and anyone who ships image models commercially

setup.requirements: Recent ComfyUI with native Krea 2 support, plus the Krea 2 text encoder (Qwen3-VL) and VAE; quantized w4a8 community builds exist for smaller GPUs

license.code: MIT (declared in the README for the fine-tune contribution only)
license.weights: Krea 2 Community License — inherited by the merged checkpoint; HF tag: krea-2-community-license
license.notes: Read carefully on 2026-08-10: the README states the fine-tune is MIT but that it 'does not grant any rights to the base weights' — and since v0.2 is a full merged checkpoint, the base weights are in the artifact. There is no LICENSE file in the repo; the metadata tag is krea-2-community-license. That license permits commercial use but binds deployers to Krea's Acceptable Use Policy and requires content-filtering or equivalent review measures — scale-independent field-of-use obligations that fail OSD #6. Per the Inkling precedent: partial. The MIT label is real, but it only covers the delta you can't separate back out.

tally.stars: 234 HF likes; w4a8 quants and LoRA Spaces multiplying on Civitai and HF

limitations: No LICENSE file in the repo means the terms live in a tag and a base-model PDF two hops away; the checkpoint requires the Krea 2 encoder stack regardless; and as a one-maintainer community project, cadence and support are best-effort.
take: A checkpoint is not a diff. Merge restricted weights into your MIT fine-tune and the restriction is what ships — this is why we read tags, not READMEs.
